beats.visual: Full-bleed screen-print scene of a period-plausible 1930s physicist's worktable with a closed wooden experiment box, loose scientific apparatus parts, and a human hand arranging the thought-experiment components; no readable writing anywhere.
beats.purpose: establish the thought experiment as a historical 1935 proposal
beats.visual_fingerprint: overhead three-quarter view of a 1930s workbench, closed wooden box centered low, period apparatus scattered around it, lone hand entering from upper edge, pale stone ground with soot-black shadows
beats.continuity: introduces the apparatus before moving inside the imagined experiment

beats.narration_slice: A cat is sealed in a box.
beats.visual: Cut inside the wooden box: a living cat crouches in the enclosed chamber while the heavy lid closes above, rendered as bold screen-print silhouettes with the surrounding enclosure filling the vertical frame.
beats.purpose: show the cat physically isolated inside the sealed box
beats.visual_fingerprint: low interior angle beside crouching cat, descending wooden lid dominating the upper frame, narrow closing shaft of light, dark enclosed box walls extending edge-to-edge
beats.continuity: moves from the exterior setup directly into the sealed interior

beats.visual: Extreme microscopic visualization of a single radioactive atom suspended against a coarse dark field, with restrained vermilion rupture marks suggesting the possibility of decay without showing a definite outcome.
beats.purpose: introduce the single microscopic radioactive uncertainty
beats.visual_fingerprint: extreme macro atom alone in a vast soot-black field, off-center nucleus with storm-blue halftone orbit forms, sparse vermilion fracture marks radiating into negative space
beats.continuity: jumps from the cat-scale enclosure to the microscopic source of uncertainty

beats.visual: Period-plausible mechanical radiation detector shown in close profile beside the tiny source chamber, its sensing element aimed toward the atom's container and linked onward by a physical wire.
beats.purpose: show that a detector monitors whether radioactive decay occurs
beats.visual_fingerprint: tight side-profile apparatus shot, detector tube occupying right half, tiny source vessel at lower left, taut wire exiting frame, oxidized-teal metal accents under broad directional light
beats.continuity: pulls back from the atom to the mechanism observing it

beats.narration_slice: Decay can trigger a poison mechanism.
beats.visual: A vermilion decay impulse reaches the detector and drives a clearly legible mechanical linkage that releases a small hammer toward a sealed poison vial, captured at the instant the trigger begins moving.
beats.purpose: show the causal chain from atomic decay to the poison apparatus
beats.visual_fingerprint: diagonal cause-and-effect composition from glowing vermilion detector contact at upper left through lever and spring to glass poison vial at lower right, machinery caught mid-motion
beats.continuity: follows the detector's physical connection into the consequence mechanism

beats.visual: Wide interior view of the box after the mechanism has fired: the poison vial is broken near the apparatus and the cat lies motionless in deep printed shadow, with the machinery receding behind it.
beats.purpose: show the macroscopic death outcome if decay triggers the mechanism
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide floor-level view across box interior, motionless cat in foreground silhouette, shattered vial and spent hammer small in distant upper corner, heavy soot-black shadow mass with sparse vermilion residue
beats.continuity: shows the completed consequence of the trigger introduced in the prior beat

beats.visual: A distinctly different high-angle view of the same conceptual box in the no-decay outcome: the poison vial remains intact, the trigger is untouched, and the alert cat stands alive beneath broad pale illumination.
beats.purpose: show the alternative macroscopic outcome when no decay occurs
beats.visual_fingerprint: high overhead corner angle, living cat standing near center with raised head, intact poison vial and dormant lever isolated along opposite wall, pale stone light covering most of the chamber
beats.continuity: contrasts the fired outcome with the untouched no-decay branch

beats.narration_slice: Quantum theory can describe both possibilities together.
beats.visual: The box interior is overlaid as two slightly misregistered screen-print states occupying the same full-bleed space: one imprint contains the standing live cat and intact mechanism while the other contains the motionless cat and fired apparatus.
beats.purpose: visually pay off how microscopic uncertainty carries into two cat-scale possibilities described together
beats.visual_fingerprint: frontal cutaway of entire box with two offset state impressions superposed in one space, storm-blue live-cat silhouette displaced upward-right and soot-black dead-cat silhouette displaced downward-left, intact and fired mechanisms likewise overlapped
beats.continuity: merges the two previously separated outcomes into one simultaneous conceptual description

beats.narration_slice: That state is called a superposition.
beats.visual: A simplified full-frame conceptual image isolates the overlapping cat states and apparatus as doubled, misregistered silhouettes within one shared box volume, emphasizing coexistence of alternatives without any labels or text.
beats.purpose: identify the combined description of alternatives as superposition
beats.visual_fingerprint: near-symmetrical straight-on composition, box walls reduced to bold outer planes, paired live/dead cat silhouettes interpenetrating at center, doubled detector and trigger forms forming a restrained teal-and-black overlap halo
beats.continuity: abstracts the combined-state image into a cleaner visual definition

beats.narration_slice: That jump from atom to cat was the point.
beats.visual: Full-bleed scale-bridge composition with a huge magnified radioactive atom dominating the lower foreground and the sealed cat box looming far above in the same continuous space; the Red Horned Everyman stands small between them, observing the visual chain from microscopic source to macroscopic consequence.
beats.purpose: emphasize that the thought experiment deliberately extends atomic uncertainty to a macroscopic cat
beats.visual_fingerprint: dramatic low-angle vertical scale composition, enormous halftone atom at bottom edge, tiny full-body horned host centered mid-distance, sealed wooden cat box towering across the upper third, vermilion causal accent threading upward between scales
beats.continuity: steps outward from the abstract superposition to reveal the deliberate microscopic-to-macroscopic scale jump
